title: Compact blob format for session offload - sketch
content:
Purpose:
A compact, forward-compatible binary/text blob format for snapshotting user sessions (KV cache + recent turns + metadata) so sessions can be offloaded from memory to disk/S3/remote cache and later restored quickly with partial or full hydration. This is a working sketch: focus is on small on-disk size, fast appendable diffs, integrity, and per-field encryption options for Private deployments.

Goals / constraints:
- Small size: minimize token-level duplication and include efficient shared-string indexing. Target: 1.5–3x compressed size vs raw token ids for active sessions.
- Fast restore: can stream-restore prefix segments without needing full blob download.
- Incremental updates: support append-only diffs to avoid rewriting large blobs frequently.
- Partial hydration: allow restoring only model-needed parts (recent-kv, system prompts) for latency-sensitive replays.
- Secure: metadata vs user content encryption separation; support envelope encryption (KMS/HSM).
- Versioned and compatible: allow older runtimes to ignore new fields gracefully.
- Simple to debug: text-friendly header + base64-friendly tooling for debugging.

High-level layout (conceptual):
[HEADER-TEXT]
MAGIC = "RI-SOFF\n"  # small printable prefix so we can cat the file in debug
VERSION: 2
SCHEMA: compact-v2
CREATED_AT: 2025-02-04T15:30:00Z
SESSION_ID: 1234-...
FLAGS: encrypted=partial,chunked=true
----
[BINARY-SEGMENT-METADATA] (length-prefixed)
- segment table: list of (segment-type, offset, length, compressed, cipher, checksum)
- segment types: STRDICT, TOKEN_IDS, KV_SNAPSHOT, RECENT_TURNS, METRICS, DIFF_INDEX
----
[BINARY SEGMENTS] (each compressed individually, optional encryption per segment)
- STRDICT: a compact shared-string dictionary keyed by small integer ids used by other segments (dedupe prompts/role names/annotations)
- TOKEN_IDS: per-turn token id sequences (varint encoded). Stores indices into STRDICT for text spans when present.
- KV_SNAPSHOT: serialized KV entries used for KV cache (key->value where value may be pointer into STRDICT or token run).
- RECENT_TURNS: compact turn list with (role_id, text_ref, token_range) pointers into STRDICT/TOKEN_IDS for minimal duplication
- DIFF_INDEX: mapping from incremental-diff id -> segment offsets (for append-only updates)

Design notes and rationale:
- STRDICT centralization: many sessions repeat system messages, assistant templates, or user signatures. Storing a per-session dictionary reduces repeated strings. Use LEB128 varints for small integers.
- Token IDs vs text blobs: prefer token ids for anything that will be re-fed to runtime (fast rehydrate). For trimmed archival we can only store text blobs (slower).
- Per-segment compression: allows quick reads of small segments (e.g., RECENT_TURNS) without decompressing entire blob. Good balance between CPU and IO.
- Optional per-segment encryption: private deployments may require specific fields (user messages) encrypted with customer CMKs; metadata and performance counters can remain unencrypted for observability.
- Checksum and integrity: each segment includes a 32-bit checksum and a 128-bit content-hash (SHA-256) in hex to verify content before restoring.

Streaming/restore patterns:
- Fast-path restore (latency sensitive): read HEADER + STRDICT + RECENT_TURNS + TOKEN_IDS partial ranges -> reconstruct active context. Only download TOKEN_IDS ranges referenced by RECENT_TURNS.
- Full restore (for debugging / analysis): download all segments in DIFF_INDEX order and replay.
- Partial restore from DIFF: use DIFF_INDEX to reconstruct snapshot at a specific diff id (useful for rollbacks/canaries).

Incremental updates and append-only diffs:
- Each new write appends new segments and a small DIFF_INDEX record with new offsets. Old segments remain unchanged so reads referencing older diff ids are stable.
- A GC compaction job can periodically rewrite blobs into a trimmed single-segment snapshot with new DIFF_INDEX and tombstone older diffs.
- Appends are atomic if we write new DIFF_INDEX and then update a small pointer in metadata (via single atomic rename or object metadata update in object stores).

Example minimal JSON-like metadata (for human readability inside header):
- active_keys: [turn:0, turn:1]
- recent_k: 64
- kv_count: 12
- encryption: {kv:cmk-123, recent_turns:none}
(Implementation note: this snippet is text-only inside HEADER; not the authoritative binary mapping which is in BINARY-SEGMENT-METADATA)

Cache keys and lookup semantics:
- Primary cache key: session_id + last_diff_id (string) -> blob location
- Secondary keys: session_id + prefix_sig (hash of last N tokens) to support prefix-level reuse across sessions (probably only for Hosted dedupe experiments)

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Partial upload failure: ensure DIFF_INDEX points only to fully uploaded segments; incomplete uploads must be garbage-collected after a TTL. Use multipart uploads with server-side commit when possible.
- Corrupted segment: verify checksums on restore; if corruption only affects deep archival segments, fall back to reconstructing from earlier DIFF_INDEX. Provide metrics (seg_corrupt_count).
- Stale diffs / race during concurrent writes: adopt optimistic CAS using object-store etag or commit-key pattern; writes that conflict must retry with latest DIFF_INDEX.

Observability & metrics to add:
- serialize_time_ms, append_size_bytes, restore_latency_95, restore_bytes_read, segment_decompress_time, segment_decrypt_time, gc_compact_duration_ms
- per-session metrics: last_offload_age_seconds, offload_frequency_per_hour

Security considerations:
- Envelope encryption per-segment; avoid encrypting STRDICT for hosted public models to allow partial dedupe cache across sessions. For Private, default to full encryption.
- Access control: blobs must be associated with tenant id and access enforced by object-store ACLs + application-level checks during restore.
- Audit: include operator id in compact header when offload initiated by admin/agent to aid audits.

Compatibility & versioning strategy:
- Header includes VERSION and SCHEMA strings. New optional segments must be added with new type names; older players must ignore unknown segment types.
- Backwards compatibility: v2 must continue to expose STRDICT/TOKEN_IDS; can add new segment types for embeddings, provenance, or hallucination-tags without breaking old readers.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Shared-dictionary cross-session dedupe vs per-session privacy implications. Could consider a server-side global dictionary for hosted to save space but requires strong privacy analysis.
- Index granularity for TOKEN_IDS: should we store per-turn ranges or per-chunk (e.g., 256-token chunks) to balance restore IO vs diff size?
- Compression algorithm: zstd level 3 is a good default; test lz4 for very fast restores.
- How large before we force compaction? policy: if total appended diffs > 5x base size or age > 24h. Need perf tests.

Developer TODOs / next steps:
- Prototype serializer/deserializer in runtime repo: runtime/pkg/offload/compact_v2.go (start with a text-first header then binary segments). PR reference: runtime PR #482 (linked above).
- Microbenchmarks: measure size and restore latency on representative sessions (chatty vs short). Add test harness scripts.
- Add unit tests for cross-version parsing & corrupted segment recovery.
- Draft KMS policy options for per-segment encryption and expose config in Private deployment helm charts.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and hybrid text/binary to ease debugging. If we prefer fully binary (faster parse) we can move header to fixed-size binary header but that increases tooling friction.
- Priority: get a working prototype that supports append-only diffs and fast partial restore. Once stable, iterate on compaction heuristics and KMS integration.

Small ascii example (very condensed):
RI-SOFF
VERSION:2
--SEG-TBL--
STRDICT @ 0x100 len=2KB c=zstd enc=none chk=...
RECENT @ 0x900 len=512B c=none enc=aesgcm chk=...
TOKIDS @ 0x1100 len=6KB c=zstd enc=none chk=...
DIFF @ 0x2600 len=128B c=none enc=none chk=...
--END--

If helpful I can: produce a small golang reference implementation sketch, produce a set of unit test vectors, or run a few sample sessions through a prototype serializer to validate sizes.

Quick decision requests for the next sync:
- pick default compression (zstd3 vs lz4)
- per-segment encryption default for Hosted vs Private
- compaction policy thresholds (differences by deployment mode)

-- end of sketch --
